images.title: Three mats, same share
images.purpose: Show that 1 roti for 2 children, 2 rotis for 4 children and 3 rotis for 6 children all give each child 1/2 of a roti.
images.composition: Three plain lunch mats in a row with wide gaps, each with its rotis and a caption, and one result line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Three plain rectangular mats in a row. Mat 1: 1 round roti cut into 2 equal halves. Mat 2: 2 round rotis, each cut into 2 equal halves. Mat 3: 3 round rotis, each cut into 2 equal halves. All rotis exactly the same size. In each mat exactly 1 half is filled reddish purple #CC79A7 to show one child's share; all other halves plain. Mat outlines teal #0072B2. Captions under each mat. No children drawn. Exactly 3 mats, 6 rotis, 12 halves, 3 purple halves.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
rotis of different sizes, or halves that are not equal
images.takeaway: Every child gets 1/2 of a roti, so 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6.
images.description: Three mats with 1, 2 and 3 rotis, every roti cut into halves, one half purple in each mat; captions give the children, and below 1/2 each and 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to point at the purple share on each mat and say it is the same size every time.

image_decisions.why: Three sharings giving the same share is easiest to see side by side; one image of three mats carries it.
